# Vehicles — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Motorbikes: typically around 125,000, most listings 45,000-240,000 (50 listings)
- Auto Parts & Accessories: typically around 1,500, most listings 500-11,000 (11 listings)
- Bicycles: typically around 5,500, most listings 1,600-46,000 (9 listings)
- Maintenance and Repair: typically around 1,300, most listings 700-3,000 (9 listings)
- Cars: typically around 1,500,000, most listings 900,000-5,200,000 (8 listings)
- Heavy Duty: typically around 500,000, most listings 400,000-1,200,000 (3 listings)

Vehicles are high-value goods: a complete bike/scooter/car priced far below the low end (e.g. a scooter listed at NPR 180 — a real case) is a scam or placeholder-price signal -> hold. For subcategories under 10 listings (Cars, Bicycles, Maintenance and Repair, Heavy Duty) the data is thin — lean on general market judgment rather than these exact bands.

## What good listings look like
- "Hyundai i10 magna-2016 model" — NPR 1,850,000
- "Honda Dio" — NPR 85,000
- "duke 200 bs4" — NPR 240,000
- "mahindra pickup 4*4" — NPR 1,350,000
- "Royal enfield connector pipe" — NPR 1,580

A good listing names brand + model (often year, engine cc, or emission standard) with a price inside the market band; parts listings name the vehicle they fit.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Token/placeholder prices on whole vehicles (NPR 100-1,000 for a bike or car). Editors' most common rejection here is "price doesn't match the actual item" — hold and let them confirm.
- Description admits missing/pending bluebook (bill book) or refuses ownership transfer, or the vehicle is Indian-registered — common stolen-vehicle / untransferable-vehicle patterns in Nepal.
- Title is a bare generic word ("vehicle", "Motor bike") with no brand/model AND an out-of-band price — insufficient to judge legitimacy.
- Obvious wrong-category items — toys posted as vehicles (real example: "Home made remote control car") — hold for recategorization.
